title: Play cut
one: Shelf's bookmark with one hole: a play cut at the notch's angle.
idea: Shelf's bookmark in paper with one play-shaped hole. The play is the notch turned forward: its slanted edges run parallel to the notch's and are as long, and it has the angle of the play button in Shelf's player, so the tail, the hole and the app's play are one shape.
built: The shared bookmark (base: 43.5 dp wide, top at 27.1, reach 32.56 of 33 dp), unchanged. The play is the notch's two halves, each 17 units across and 11 up, joined along their 17-unit sides: its flat side is twice the notch's depth (28.15 dp) and its depth half the bookmark's width (21.75 dp), so depth = height × 17/22 and both slanted edges are parallel to the notch (32.9 degrees; the app's Lucide play is 32.7). The flat side is 12.2 dp from the left edge and the drawn tip 11.2 dp from the right; a point carries less weight than a flat side, so these look equal. The axis is at y 49.8, 2.9 dp below the middle of the body (round one's p2 was 4.5 dp below), which leaves 10.2 dp of paper above and a 7.6 dp strap along the notch, parallel to it; the play's lowest point is 4.5 dp above the notch's apex. The hole is 15% of the bookmark. B's play has the same axis and shape, larger.
corners: Matched by angle, the same rule in A and B. Corners as acute as the tail tips take the tips' radius, 1.5/34 of the bookmark's width (1.92 dp): the play's back corners have exactly the tips' angle (57 degrees) and its point is 66. Right angles take the shoulders' 4/34: 5.12 dp on the bookmark, and 4/34 of a bar's width on B's pause. Shelf's bookmark already works this way: its shoulders and its tips both round off 2.1 dp inside their sharp points. Compared with p1's 3.1 dp at 1x and 4x: on a 1x home screen the two can't be told apart; at 4x 3.1 dp looks softer than the tail tips beside it and closer to Play Books' rounded play, so the tips' radius stays. On the cuts the play keeps that radius, scaled to the cut's bookmark (1.24 px at 48, 0.88 at 32, 0.71 on the glyph), while base draws the cuts' tail tips sharp on pixel corners, so at those sizes the play's corners are a little softer than the tips. Drawn sharp, the play's back corners fall inside pixels and each leaves a stray part-tone pixel (52 soft pixels against 50 at 48, 42 against 39 at 32), so the rounding stays there too.
small: Every cut is base's bookmark, unchanged. At 48 and 32 px and on the glyph the play is built from that cut's own notch, so it stays parallel to it; at 16 px it is drawn in whole pixels. 48 px: 18 × 14 px (the folded notch exactly), flat side on x 18 with 8 px of paper there, 7 at the tip, 6 above and a 4.9 px strap (the master's 7.6 dp at this scale); its axis is on y 21, a pixel boundary, so its corners land on whole pixels and its two slanted edges are mirror images; 6.9% soft, against the plain bookmark's 3.3. 32 px: 13.5 × 10.4 px on x 11, half a pixel taller than the folded notch, which on whole pixels sits to one side; 5 and 5.4 px at the sides, 4 above, a 3.35 px strap; 10.7% soft (plain 5.2). Whole-pixel stairs were tried at 32 and look like pixel art beside the notch's smooth diagonal. 16 px: p1's whole-pixel play, columns of 5, 3, 3 and 1 from x 6 on rows 4 to 8, with 3 px at each side, 2 above and 2 over the notch's apex, so nothing leaks into the notch; it adds no part-tone pixels (12.2% soft, all from the bookmark's own corners and notch). Glyph: 11 × 8.8 px on x 8, a pixel taller than the folded notch, which sits to the left on whole pixels; its axis is on y 10.5, the middle of a pixel row, so its corners land on whole pixels (y 5 and 16) and the rows either side of the tip are mirror images. 4 and 3.8 px at the sides, 3.6 above and a 3 px strap; 13% soft (plain 6.3). Every size keeps the play.
risks: Google Play Books pairs the same two signs, and GoodLinks, an Apple-only read-later app, is a white notched bookmark with a symbol in its body. Shelf's square shoulders, the single colour and a cut hole rather than a stamped symbol keep it apart, but among media apps a bookmark with a play can read as a podcast or audiobook app. The rhyme with the notch shows on the launcher; at toolbar sizes this is simply a bookmark with a play. On the launcher the play's corners are crisp beside the round shoulders, on purpose, because they match the tail tips. The extension's toolbar button only saves, so a play there promises listening the extension doesn't offer; base's plain bookmark could stand in for the toolbar cuts.
